A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have cloned, sequenced, and characterized a new insect globin gene.
the pC-S-9 gene is an example of an ancient globin gene, and that the Chironomidae have retained a gene that is not present in the Drosophila melanogaster genome.
the pC-S7 and pC-S9 cDNA clones represent two members of the Hb VIIB subfamily, which is the most recently evolved of the four globin subfamilies in the Chironomidae.
The main takeaway from our work is that
synthetic oligonucleotids, which are easily prepared and are inexpensive, are powerful tools for isolating and identifying genes from cDNA banks.
the globin VI subfamily has a much larger number of members than was previously thought.
a single synthetic oligonucleotide, designed to hybridize with the 3' end of a globin mRNA, can be used to isolate a cDNA clone that contains most of the coding region for an uncharacterized globin.
